auth_boundary_surface_label: Example State official voter-information public-read and sign-in boundary policy
delivery_role_note: Public-read boundaries distinguish anonymously readable general voter-information routes from genuinely customized or private functions, but they do not replace content correctness, identity assurance, or ordinary help routing.
public_read_boundary_note: General read-only voter-information routes remain anonymously readable and do not require account creation or sign-in.
auth_requirement_reason_note: Routes that require authentication state what private or customized function the sign-in unlocks instead of presenting sign-in as a generic front door.
anonymous_help_and_explanation_note: When a private route requires sign-in, the page still exposes a public explanation of the boundary and the ordinary official help/contact lane without authentication.
session_timeout_and_warning_note: Authentication timeouts warn users in advance and offer a clear way to continue or reauthenticate before work is lost.
reauthentication_context_preservation_no: When reauthentication is required, the office preserves in-progress state or returns the user to the same task context when feasible.
public_route_login_replacement_avoidance: Public answer routes do not quietly resolve to sign-in shells, expired-session pages, or dead account gates in place of the current official answer.
crawler_visibility_boundary_note: Publicly readable answer routes remain accessible to crawlers and anonymous users; private routes are intentionally separate and not relied on as the main public discovery landing page.
